25503.old: In Highcharts, a polygon chart is a Cartesian chart that uses the polygon series type to draw a filled, freeform shape through a list of [x, y] points. It is useful for showing a target range or region next to observed data points, and is often combined with a scatter series. This post walks through creating one in four steps: load the scripts, add a container, style it, and initialize the chart.
25503.new: A polygon chart draws a filled, freeform shape through a set of points, which makes it useful for showing a target range or region next to the data you have actually observed. It is often combined with a scatter series, so readers can see at a glance which points fall inside the area and which fall outside. This post walks through creating one with Highcharts, step by step.

25396.old: To plot latitude and longitude on a map with Highcharts® Maps, load a base map in GeoJSON or TopoJSON format, create a mapChart, and add a mappoint series whose data points have lat and lon properties. This tutorial builds an interactive map of nine UK cities with tooltips, zoom and pan, and shares best-practice tips along the way.
25396.new: Plotting latitude and longitude on a map turns rows of coordinates into something people can read at a glance: where things are, how they cluster and how far apart they lie. This tutorial builds an interactive map of nine UK cities with Highcharts® Maps, with tooltips, zoom and pan, and shares best-practice tips along the way.

26169.old: A box and whisker plot (boxplot) summarizes a data distribution with five values: minimum, first quartile (Q1), median, third quartile (Q3) and maximum. It shows spread, skewness and potential outliers at a glance, which makes it useful in fields from scientific research to financial analysis. In Highcharts, you create one by loading highcharts.js and highcharts-more.js and setting chart.type to 'boxplot', as this post shows step by step.
26169.new: A box and whisker plot (boxplot) summarizes a data distribution with five values: minimum, first quartile (Q1), median, third quartile (Q3) and maximum. It shows spread, skewness and potential outliers at a glance, which makes it useful in fields from scientific research to financial analysis. This post explains how to read a box plot and how to create one with Highcharts, step by step.

26592.old: IoT weather stations collect large amounts of data on temperature, wind, precipitation and more, and that data is hard to use without good visualization. This tutorial shows how to build an interactive live weather dashboard with Highcharts® Dashboards: a station map, KPI gauges, a forecast grid and a forecast chart, fed by MET Norway forecast data through a JSON data connector. It covers layout, component configuration, dark mode, responsive CSS and how to swap in your own IoT data source.
26592.new: IoT weather stations collect large amounts of data on temperature, wind, precipitation and more, and that data is hard to use without good visualization. This tutorial shows how to build an interactive live weather dashboard with Highcharts® Dashboards: a station map, KPI gauges, a forecast grid and a forecast chart, fed by live forecast data from MET Norway. It covers layout, components, dark mode, responsive design and how to connect your own IoT data source.

25269.old: Real-time data visualization lets you follow financial markets, live scores or server health as they happen. Highcharts supports it in two ways: the data module with polling, which needs only configuration (a data source and a refresh interval), or API methods that update the chart programmatically from WebSockets, AJAX calls or any custom data source. This post explains both and walks through a live CSV polling example step by step.
25269.new: Real-time data visualization lets you follow financial markets, live scores or server health as they happen, so people can react while it still matters. Highcharts can keep a chart up to date in two ways: by checking a data source at regular intervals, or by pushing new values to the chart as they arrive. This post explains both and walks through a live example step by step.

25535.old: Lightning strikes about 100 times per second worldwide, and static maps cannot capture data that changes this fast. To create an interactive lightning map with Highcharts® Maps, load a base map such as Europe, add a mapbubble series for the strikes, color each strike by age with a colorAxis, and drive playback with a range input and a play/pause button. This tutorial recreates the official demo using historical strike data from frost.met.no.
25535.new: Lightning strikes about 100 times per second worldwide, and static maps cannot capture data that changes this fast. An interactive lightning map shows where and when strikes happen, with each strike colored by its age and a timeline you can play, pause and scrub through. This tutorial recreates the official Highcharts® Maps demo using historical strike data from frost.met.no.

26178.old: A network graph shows relationships as nodes (points) connected by edges (lines), revealing clusters, hierarchies and key influencers that are hard to see in a table. In Highcharts, you build one by loading highcharts.js and modules/networkgraph.js, setting chart.type to 'networkgraph', and passing from/to pairs as series data. Highcharts then positions the nodes with a force-directed layout, and users can drag them to explore relationships.
26178.new: A network graph shows relationships as nodes (points) connected by edges (lines), revealing clusters, hierarchies and key influencers that are hard to see in a table. The nodes arrange themselves so that closely connected items end up near each other, and readers can drag them around to explore how everything is linked. This post covers the key components of a network graph and how to create one with Highcharts.

30125.old: Users expect the same chart experience on desktop, tablet, mobile and in print. Highcharts keeps charts consistent across all of them by using one configuration and theme for brand colors and fonts, responsive.rules breakpoints to adapt layout to screen size, and the exporting module to produce static PNG or PDF output for print. For multi-component interfaces, Highcharts Dashboards adds a Flexbox-based layout engine that repositions charts, KPI gauges and data grids across screen sizes.
30125.new: Users expect the same chart experience on desktop, tablet, mobile and in print. Highcharts keeps charts consistent across all of them: one setup carries your brand colors and fonts everywhere, the layout adapts to the screen size, and charts can be exported as static images or PDFs for print. For multi-component interfaces, Highcharts Dashboards repositions charts, KPI gauges and data grids automatically across screen sizes.

26509.old: A dependency wheel is a type of chord diagram that shows directed, weighted relationships between entities arranged around a circle, which makes complex flows easier to read than in traditional charts. In Highcharts, you create one by loading highcharts.js plus the sankey.js and dependency-wheel.js modules, then adding a series of type 'dependencywheel' with data in a from, to, weight format. This post shows how, step by step.
26509.new: A dependency wheel is a type of chord diagram that shows relationships between entities arranged around a circle. The width of each ribbon shows how strong a connection is and which way it flows, which makes complex flows such as trade, migration or dependencies easier to read than in traditional charts. This post explains how to read one and how to create it with Highcharts.

26473.old: 3D charts catch attention, but they can also distort data. Use a 3D chart only when your data has three meaningful dimensions or when interactive rotation helps users explore it. Otherwise choose a 2D chart, because perspective distortion, occlusion and extra cognitive load can mislead readers. This post covers when 3D works, when it fails, and how to build 3D charts in Highcharts with the highcharts-3d.js module, including rotatable 3D scatter plots.
26473.new: 3D charts catch attention, but they can also distort data. Use a 3D chart only when your data has three meaningful dimensions or when interactive rotation helps users explore it. Otherwise choose a 2D chart, because perspective distortion, hidden data points and extra mental effort can mislead readers. This post covers when 3D works, when it fails, and how to build 3D charts with Highcharts, including a rotatable 3D scatter plot.

25292.old: Big data visualization turns large datasets into charts where trends, patterns and outliers are easy to spot. Highcharts handles it by combining the Boost module, which uses WebGL to offload rendering to the GPU, with interactive zooming and panning and asynchronous data loading. The demos in this post render 500,000 to 1.7 million data points, including a 1-million-point scatter chart and a 1.7-million-point AAPL stock chart.
25292.new: Big data visualization turns large datasets into charts where trends, patterns and outliers are easy to spot. Highcharts can draw hundreds of thousands of points smoothly in the browser, while readers zoom, pan and load more detail as they go. The demos in this post show 500,000 to 1.7 million data points, including a 1-million-point scatter chart and a 1.7-million-point AAPL stock chart.

26512.old: A standard deviation graph shows how far data points spread around the mean, typically as a bell curve with intervals marked in σ. A low standard deviation means values cluster near the mean; a high one means they are spread out. This guide covers its applications in statistical analysis and data science, and how to build one in Highcharts with the bellcurve series from the histogram-bellcurve module.
26512.new: A standard deviation graph shows how far data points spread around the mean, typically as a bell curve with intervals marked in σ. A low standard deviation means values cluster near the mean; a high one means they are spread out. This guide covers its applications in statistical analysis and data science, and how to create a bell curve chart with Highcharts.

26146.old: A waterfall chart shows how a starting value is increased and decreased by a series of positive and negative steps until it reaches a final total. To read one, start at the first bar, follow each floating bar up or down from where the previous bar ended, and compare the result with the subtotal and final sum bars. In Highcharts, you create one by setting chart.type to 'waterfall' and loading highcharts-more.js, as this post shows.
26146.new: A waterfall chart shows how a starting value is increased and decreased by a series of positive and negative steps until it reaches a final total. To read one, start at the first bar, follow each floating bar up or down from where the previous bar ended, and compare the result with the subtotal and final sum bars. This post explains where waterfall charts are useful and how to create one with Highcharts.

25625.old: Default chart styles can clash with your brand's design. You can customize Highcharts to match your brand by overriding the default colors, fonts and chart styles in the chart options, reusing them through themes, or moving all styling into CSS with styled mode. Pattern fills, gradients and shadows add further visual control. This guide covers each approach with live examples.
25625.new: Default chart styles can clash with your brand's design. You can customize Highcharts to match your brand by changing the default colors, fonts and chart styles, reusing them as themes across all your charts, or controlling the look with your own CSS. Pattern fills, gradients and shadows add further visual control. This guide covers each approach with live examples.

25468.old: Geospatial data, from sales locations to environmental change, is hard to use without the right visualization tools. Highcharts® Maps builds interactive geographic maps in JavaScript: it loads map geometry from GeoJSON or TopoJSON, or uses tiled web maps from external providers, and joins your data to map regions with the joinBy option. It supports choropleth, point and line maps with zoom, pan and tooltips, and this post helps you get started.
25468.new: Geospatial data, from sales locations to environmental change, is hard to use without the right visualization tools. Highcharts® Maps turns it into interactive maps where regions are colored by value and points and lines mark places and routes, with zoom, pan and tooltips for exploring the details. This post explains the common map types and helps you get started.

25312.old: A Pareto chart combines a bar chart and a line chart: the bars show individual categories in descending order and the line shows their cumulative percentage, so you can see which few factors cause most of the effect. It builds on the Pareto principle (the 80/20 rule), named after the Italian economist Vilfredo Pareto. In Highcharts, you build one with the pareto module and a series of type pareto, as this post shows.
25312.new: A Pareto chart combines a bar chart and a line chart: the bars show individual categories in descending order and the line shows their cumulative percentage, so you can see which few factors cause most of the effect. It builds on the Pareto principle (the 80/20 rule), named after the Italian economist Vilfredo Pareto. This post explains how to read a Pareto chart and how to create one with Highcharts.

31210.old: A predictive analytics visualization shows forecast values alongside historical data and confidence intervals, so stakeholders can judge both the prediction and its uncertainty. In Highcharts, you separate history from forecast with zones (for example, solid versus dotted lines), mark the transition with a plot line, and show uncertainty with shaded range bands.
31210.new: A predictive analytics visualization shows forecast values alongside historical data and confidence intervals, so stakeholders can judge both the prediction and its uncertainty. A good forecast chart makes it obvious where the known data ends and the prediction begins, for example with solid versus dotted lines, a marker at the transition and shaded bands that show the range of likely outcomes.

25917.old: To map the top 100 US cities with Highcharts® Maps, combine a tiledwebmap series (OpenStreetMap provider, Web Mercator projection) with a mapbubble series whose points use lat, lon and a z value for population. Bubble size reflects population, and a tooltip shows each city’s name, state abbreviation and population. Tile-based mapping keeps the map fast and scalable, even with large datasets.
25917.new: A map of the top 100 US cities shows at a glance where people live: each city is a bubble sized by its population, placed on a detailed, zoomable background map. Hovering over a bubble shows the city’s name, state and population. This post shows how to build the map with Highcharts® Maps, which stays fast and scalable even with large datasets.

26276.old: A market depth chart plots the cumulative volume of buy orders (bids) and sell orders (asks) at each price level, showing market liquidity and where supply and demand concentrate. In Highcharts, you build one as an area chart with step: 'center', two series (bids and asks) of [price, cumulative volume] points, and a plot line marking the current price. This article explains how depth charts work, what they reveal about market dynamics, and how to implement them.
26276.new: A market depth chart plots the cumulative volume of buy orders (bids) and sell orders (asks) at each price level, showing market liquidity and where supply and demand concentrate. The two sides meet at the current price, so traders can see how much buying or selling it would take to move the market. This article explains how depth charts work, what they reveal about market dynamics, and how to create one with Highcharts.

26498.old: A radar chart (also called a polar or spider chart) plots three or more quantitative variables on axes that start from the same center point. It works best for comparing a few entities across 5-8 related metrics on a shared scale, and can confuse more than it clarifies when used for the wrong data. This guide covers when radar charts work, when to avoid them, and how to build one in Highcharts by loading highcharts-more.js and setting chart.polar to true.
